source.title: Low Curvature Activations Reduce Overfitting in Adversarial Training
source.authors: Vasu Singla; Sahil Singla; S. Feizi; David W. Jacobs

record.tranche_reason: The study reports results that refine generalization-gap claims for adversarially trained networks: activation curvature changes the gap, and the width-related double-descent result differs by activation. Its setting does not test the listed versions’ standard-training claims.
record.gate_note: The study tests adversarially trained classifiers on natural image labels, not networks trained with standard empirical-risk methods. Its results therefore fit none of V1–V8 as written. Reported comparisons of final and best-validation checkpoints are included only when they measure a generalization gap; cited prior-work results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures activation-dependent generalization gaps and width-dependent robust test error under adversarial training. None directly tests V1–V8. In particular, Figure 7 does not identify the width needed for zero training error or establish improvement beyond that threshold, as V2 requires. Activation curvature and input-Hessian eigenvalues also differ from V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: low exact or approximate activation curvature reduces standard and robust generalization gaps and largely mitigates robust overfitting and width-related double descent during adversarial training. This is not a claim of uniformly improved test accuracy, and the authors do not prove a monotonic relationship between activation curvature and robustness.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adversarial training with PGD attacks and varies activation curvature; the listed versions concern standard training or other interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function and curvature; PSwish β; LeakyReLU slope k; dataset; width factor and activation in the double-descent sweep; training checkpoint (final versus best validation checkpoint).

fits_no_version.finding: Lower exact or approximate activation curvature accompanies smaller standard and robust train-to-test gaps in adversarially trained ResNet-18 models. Smaller gaps need not mean higher test accuracy: PSwish β=0.5 has a 1.76-point robust gap and 45.24% robust test accuracy, versus a 38.57-point gap and 50.63% accuracy at β=10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation curvature affects fitting and generalization gaps during adversarial training, with a tradeoff between gap reduction and test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report width-related robust-error double descent for ReLU but no such peak for SiLU in adversarially trained Wide ResNet-28 models. They state that SiLU at width factor 4 matches ReLU at 15, while their performance becomes equivalent at large widths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice can mitigate a width-related double-descent peak under adversarial training, with diminishing advantage at large widths.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The authors state that they do not rigorously prove a monotonic relationship between robustness and activation curvature. The width-sweep experiment reports averages for the last 3 epochs, but no uncertainty estimates are stated. The results concern adversarial training and do not establish the listed standard-training claims.

untested.parts: No paired natural-label and random-label fitting and held-out evaluation.
No demonstration of continued test-error improvement beyond the width needed for zero training error; the sweep uses adversarially trained, regularized Wide ResNet-28 models.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison; batch size is fixed at 128.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, gap-ranking evaluation, or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: T6 is relative to the specified versions, despite the study's original experiments on adjacent generalization questions. All rows retain versions=["none"]; cannot_determine indicates that their measures cannot establish any listed version, not that their reported gaps are unreadable. No listed-version results require missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under standard training.
The width sweep uses adversarial training, not the specified standard training of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch study.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization measures.
